articles.summary: Global atmospheric dust levels have declined since 2003, according to a study by Gupta et al. published in *Science Advances* (2026). Despite a massive “Godzilla” dust storm that carried Saharan dust to the Americas in 2020, the long-term trend shows Earth’s atmosphere has become less dusty over the past couple of decades. The findings, highlighted in *Nature*, are based on satellite observations and climate modeling.

At room temperature, atoms hum with thermal energy and appear blurry in images, but at ultra-cold temperatures, near absolute zero (0 kelvin), they come almost to a standstill and can even adopt strange quantum behaviours. articles.summary: Bruker, based in Billerica, Massachusetts, will ship the first scanning transmission electron microscope with built-in liquid helium cooling — called GAIA — to laboratories in Canada, Germany, and the United States by early next year. The instrument can cool samples to near absolute zero, drastically reducing atomic thermal motion and enabling stable atomic-resolution imaging for extended periods. Last year, U.S. researchers demonstrated a similar cooling attachment that reached 20 kelvin (−253 °C) and maintained atomic-resolution imaging for over ten hours. A tiny two-headed turtle weighing less than a nickel ended up at the Cape Cod facility. The bicephalic (two-headed) reptile is a diamondback terrapin (Malaclemys terrapin), aquatic turtles found in brackish waters along the United States’ Atlantic and Gulf coasts. articles.summary: A tiny two-headed diamondback terrapin weighing less than a nickel has been transferred to the Cape Wildlife Center after hatching in a protected nesting site in Wellfleet, Cape Cod. The species is classified as Threatened under the Massachusetts Endangered Species Act, with its federal conservation status currently under review. articles.summary: In March 2026, Google announced that quantum computers could break common encryption methods by the end of the decade, potentially exposing personal data, state secrets, and financial accounts. The company warned that governments and digital stewards must urgently adopt more secure online systems, though this transition is complex and costly. The article, published on September 22, 2026, in Scientific American, explores the implications of this breakthrough for digital security.

articles.summary: Scientists have discovered the largest new impact crater in the solar system on the moon, named McGetchin Crater after geologist Tom McGetchin. The crater, spanning more than two football fields wide, was identified by Robert Wagner of Intuitive Machines while comparing Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter images from May 2024 and April 2024. This finding, located on the moon's eastern edge, underscores the importance of ongoing lunar surveillance, as the orbiter has monitored the moon for 17 years.

articles.title: Even morning coffee might mess with your sleep
articles.description: Even your usual morning coffee routine may disrupt your night's sleep. Credit: Boy Anupong via Getty Images Coffee drinkers often fall into two groups—those who refuse another cup past a certain time of day, and those who are happy to grab a refill well into the night. The people who practice restraint frequently cite mounting evidence of caffeine’s effects on your sleep cycle, while freewheeling coffee chuggers say they have no problem going to bed after their post-dinner espresso. Unfortunately, a recent study is likely to annoy people on both sides of the argument. According to medical rese
articles.summary: A study from Wroclaw University in Poland, published in the journal Nutrients, found that caffeine from coffee may impair sleep quality even when consumed in the morning. Researchers used electroencephalography (EEG) scans during a clinical sleep experiment to measure detailed brain activity, revealing reduced slow‑wave activity — a key marker of deep, restorative sleep — regardless of consumption time. Study co‑author Donata Kurpas, a family medicine specialist, explained that EEG allows observation of “how the brain is sleeping” and detects subtle changes missed by standard sleep assessments

articles.summary: NASA-funded researchers have discovered Incendiamoeba cascadensis, a heat-loving amoeba in California's Lassen Volcanic National Park, that reproduces at 145°F (63°C), setting a new upper temperature limit for known eukaryotes. The fire amoeba remains motile up to 147°F (64°C) and can recover from brief exposure to 158°F (70°C), surpassing the previous eukaryotic record of 140°F (60°C). This breakthrough challenges assumptions about the thermal limits of complex cellular life and has implications for the search for life beyond Earth. The findings were reported by NASA on September 22, 2026.

covered.coreFact: Огляд розглядає, чи зможуть нейроморфні комп’ютери наблизитися до енергоефективності мозку, який споживає близько 20 ватів; нинішні AI-системи потребують значно більше енергії.

covered.subject: Як пережити спеку й посуху
covered.coreFact: Редакційний матеріал обговорює екстремальну спеку, тривалі посухи та спекулятивну ідею постачання сонячного світла на вимогу; це огляд проблем і можливих підходів, а не нове дослідження.

covered.subject: Пульсар захоплює зоряний вітер
covered.coreFact: XRISM безпосередньо зафіксував, як пульсар у системі BP Crucis захоплює вітер блакитного гіпергіганта; це дає змогу точніше вивчати акрецію на компактні об’єкти.

covered.subject: Телескоп Roman побачив перше світло
covered.coreFact: Телескоп NASA Nancy Grace Roman 11 вересня зафіксував перші фотони зоряного світла; це важливий етап підготовки до оглядів темної енергії, темної матерії та екзопланет.

covered.subject: Мегапосуха на південному заході США
covered.coreFact: Мегапосуха на південному заході США триває близько 27 років і вже спричинила різке скорочення водопостачання в Аризоні; регіон переживає найсухіший період приблизно за 1200 років.

covered.subject: Мозок формують дві лінії клітин-попередників
covered.coreFact: Дослідження припускає, що мозок формують дві окремі популяції клітин-попередників: одна дає початок задньому мозку, інша — передньому та середньому; висновок ще оскаржують деякі науковці.

covered.subject: Нові докази прихованих камер біля гробниці Тутанхамона
covered.coreFact: Нові дані геофізичного обстеження посилюють підозру щодо порожнин за гробницею Тутанхамона, але не підтверджують існування камер чи поховання Нефертіті.
